factsheet.heading: The Tour
paragraphs: An unofficial walking tour of the secret locations used to film the Star Wars franchise! Uncover why the famous movies could never have been made without London. Hear about the crucial role the city played in three different empires, Roman, British, and Galactic!

Discover how London's Barbican Estate was the perfect shooting location for a dystopian view of the science fiction city, and the beating heart of the Empire: Coruscant. (As seen in the TV series ANDOR)

But this isn't just a film tour. You will explore the real-world history of London. Discover the ancient origins of the city, how it was rebuilt from the ashes of WWII, how it adapted to the 21st century, and how its venerable and ancient customs still determine the fate of the city today.
Part Star Wars adventure, part architectural tour, part history lesson: Prepare to jump into hyperspace and discover how London and the destiny of Star Wars  are so deeply intertwined!

factsheet.heading: The History
paragraphs: We will explore the Barbican, Alban Gate and the London Guildhall.

The Barbican in London spans from Roman fortifications to a post-war Brutalist masterpiece. Heavily damaged during the 1940 Blitz, the area was transformed in the 1960s and 1970s into a visionary residential estate and arts hub designed to bring people back to live in the heart of the city.

Alban Gate, located at 125 London Wall, is a major Postmodern office complex in the City of London. Designed by Terry Farrell & Company and built between 1990 and 1992, it replaced a 1960s block named Lee House and defined an exuberant peak of 1980s architectural design.

The London Guildhall is the ceremonial and administrative hub of the City of London. Built between 1411 and 1440, its medieval Great Hall is the oldest secular stone structure surviving in the City. It has hosted royal banquets, major state trials, and civic governance for over 600 years.

factsheet.heading: Clothing and Footwear Requirement
paragraphs: Wear comfortable footwear and clothes. Dress for the weather.  And bring water or snacks if desired.

travel_info: Additional travel info: The tour finishes at the London Guildhall near Moorgate or Bank Station. Also a slightly longer walk from St Paul's
